belongs_to: Deep Dive (book p.134): two square running tracks with a common finishing line, race of 350 m; printed answer 'From point A to flag: 100 + 100 + 100 + 50 = 350 m; From point B to flag: 125 + 150 + 75 = 350 m'
description: Two concentric squares (a double running track) drawn with thin black outlines on white, plus red arrows, a flagpole with two flags and points A and B. OUTER square: side labelled '150 m' (the label sits just above the top side, slightly left of its middle). INNER square: side labelled '100 m' (label sits inside the inner square, just under its top side, a little left of the middle). The inner square is centred in the outer one, so the lane between them has the same width (about one third of the inner side) on all four sides. POINT B: a black dot on the TOP side of the outer square, about 80% of the way from its left corner to its right corner (near the top-right), letter 'B' just above-right of the dot. POINT A: a black dot at the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner of the inner square, letter 'A' just below-right of the dot. FINISHING LINE: one vertical black line (the flagpole) at about 44% of the inner bottom side measured from the inner bottom-left corner (about the middle of the outer bottom side). It starts inside the inner square a little above the inner square's bottom side (about one third of the inner side above it), runs down through the inner bottom side and the bottom lane, crosses the outer square's bottom side and ends below the outer square. FLAGS: two small right-pointing triangular flags attached to the pole, each with a flat top edge on the pole's right side: an ORANGE flag inside the inner square just above the inner bottom side, and a GREEN flag directly below it in the bottom lane (between the inner bottom side and the outer bottom side). LABEL: the text 'Common Finishing Line' under the bottom end of the pole, with a short black arrow from the text pointing up-left to the pole. ARROWS (4 solid red arrows with dark outline, showing the running direction, anticlockwise): in the TOP lane one arrow pointing LEFT, near the middle of the top lane; in the LEFT lane one arrow pointing DOWN, near the vertical middle of the left lane; in the RIGHT lane one arrow pointing UP, near the vertical middle of the right lane; and one arrow pointing RIGHT drawn inside the inner square just above its bottom side, to the left of the pole and pointing at the pole (it is not in the bottom lane). No other numbers, no start positions are marked by the book in this printed picture except the dots A and B.
unclear: Exact dot positions of A and B and of the pole are only approximate (read from the picture; the book's answer implies the flag is 50 m from the inner bottom-left corner and 75 m from the outer bottom-left corner, i.e. at the middle of the outer bottom side)
The bottom red arrow lies inside the inner square rather than in the bottom lane; it is drawn that way in the book

belongs_to: Figure it Out p.145, Q 'Using 9 unit squares, solve the following', part 3: 'Make a figure with a perimeter of 18 units' (printed answer '3.' is this picture)
description: A connected figure made of exactly 9 unit squares (black outlines, white fill, no shading), arranged in 3 rows on a grid of 6 columns (columns numbered 1 to 6 from the left). TOP row: 2 squares in columns 3 and 4. MIDDLE row: 4 squares in columns 3, 4, 5 and 6 (a horizontal strip of 4). BOTTOM row: 3 squares in columns 1, 2 and 3. So the first square of the top row, the first square of the middle row and the last square of the bottom row are all in column 3, stacked directly one above another (the figure is joined there); the middle row's squares 2 to 4 extend right and the top row's second square sits above the middle row's second square; the bottom row extends left from column 3. Counting check: 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 squares; 9 shared edges between neighbouring squares; perimeter = 4 x 9 - 2 x 9 = 18 units. MEASUREMENT LABELS (plain black text with double-headed arrows): above the top-left square of the figure (the column 3 square of the top row) a double-headed arrow with the text '1 Unit' (spans exactly one square width); below the bottom row a double-headed arrow with the text '3 Units' (spans the full width of the 3 bottom squares, columns 1 to 3). No perimeter number or other label is printed in the picture.
